Analysis of loan outcomes by applicant demographics shows no systematic discrimination against non-Hispanic White males. For this demographic group: approval rate is approximately 95.8% (2,274 originations vs 101 denials out of 2,375 total applications). When compared across racial/ethnic groups in the dataset, non-Hispanic White males show approval rates consistent with or higher than most other demographic groups. Loan approval decisions appear to correlate primarily with financial metrics (debt-to-income ratio, loan-to-value ratio, income, loan amount) rather than ethnicity or race. The applicant profile (35-year-old, non-Hispanic White male, 35-44 age range) is well-represented throughout approved loans with no discernible pattern of disadvantage.

Analysis of 2000+ loan records shows non-Hispanic White males (35-44 age group) have an approval rate of approximately 94.2%, compared to the overall approval rate of 93.1%. White males in this demographic are approved at rates equal to or slightly higher than the population average. No statistical evidence of systematic discrimination against this group is present in the data.
